title: Explain Information Technology
points: Understand IT as the use of computing and communication technologies to collect, process, store, retrieve and communicate information.
Recognise that IT combines computer systems, communications and information processing.

title: Distinguish major computer-system types
points: Compare supercomputers, mainframes, desktops, mobile devices and embedded systems.
Use processing speed, storage and portability when deciding which system is suitable.

title: Explain major hardware components
points: Explain the roles of input devices, CPU, RAM, ROM, secondary storage and output devices.
Recognise common secondary-storage devices and storage units.

title: Explain how hardware components interrelate
points: Follow data through the Input → Processing → Output cycle.
Explain how storage supports the cycle by keeping data, instructions and results.

title: Evaluate cloud and local storage
points: Compare capacity, cost, accessibility and security.
Choose an appropriate storage approach for a scenario and justify the decision.

title: Select input and output devices
points: Match devices such as OMR, OCR, MICR, scanners, sensors, biometrics and touchscreens to suitable applications.
Choose appropriate visual and audible output devices including printers, plotters, 3D printers and audio devices.

title: Explain the role of software
points: Distinguish system software from application software.
Recognise general-purpose, special-purpose, integrated, off-the-shelf, custom-written and customised software.

title: Discuss user-interface types
points: Compare command-line, menu-driven, graphical and touch interfaces.
Consider usability and suitability for different users and tasks.

title: Evaluate computer suitability
points: Judge CPU, RAM, secondary storage, software and I/O devices against a stated purpose.
Apply the criteria to gaming, browsing, graphics, video editing and desktop publishing.

title: Troubleshoot basic hardware problems
points: Check cables, monitor controls, printer consumables and batteries before assuming a major fault.
Use a simple, logical troubleshooting sequence.

title: Distinguish data and information
points: Treat data as raw facts and information as processed, useful data.
Recognise sources and document forms including human-readable, machine-readable, hard copy, soft copy and turnaround documents.

title: Evaluate online information
points: Check authenticity, currency, relevance and bias.
Use more than one factor before deciding whether an online source is dependable.

title: Differentiate validation and verification
points: Validation checks whether data follows rules.
Verification checks whether data was entered or copied accurately.

title: Choose validation and verification checks
points: Use range, reasonableness, data type, consistency, presence, format and length checks appropriately.
Use double entry and proofreading as verification methods.

title: Select file organisation and access
points: Distinguish sequential, serial, direct and random access.
Choose an approach for applications such as archiving, payroll and real-time systems.

title: Distinguish types of networks
points: Compare LAN, MAN, WAN and mobile networks.
Recognise Bluetooth, Wi-Fi and hotspots, and distinguish Internet, intranet and extranet privacy levels.
Understand the broad development of mobile networks from earlier generations to current systems without requiring internal technical detail.

title: Explain basic network components
points: Explain wired media such as twisted pair, coaxial and fibre.
Explain wireless media such as infrared, microwave and satellite.
Explain the roles of switches, routers, modems and network interface cards.

title: Assess mobile communication
points: Judge the usefulness of mobile networks for education, commerce and journalism.
Consider mobility, reach, speed of communication and practical limitations.

title: Explain Web technology concepts
points: Connect WWW, HTML, HTTP, hyperlinks, web servers, web pages, browsers, URLs, FTP, upload/download and email.
Explain how these concepts work together when a user accesses or transfers online information.

title: Outline computer security and misuse
points: Understand vulnerability, threat, attack and countermeasure.
Relate cybersecurity to identifying and reducing risk.

title: Assess the impact of computer misuse
points: Recognise cyberbullying, copyright infringement, data theft, denial-of-service, malware, identity theft, phishing, piracy, privacy violations, electronic eavesdropping and industrial espionage.
Consider effects on individuals, organisations and governments.

title: Describe security countermeasures
points: Use backup/recovery, firewalls, intrusion detection, biometrics, authentication, encryption and anti-malware appropriately.
Practise safer email, URL checking, Wi-Fi use, mobile-device security and social-media behaviour.

title: Assess automation and job security
points: Consider both job loss and productivity gains.
Recognise that automation can change skill requirements and create a need for retraining.

title: Describe computer-related careers
points: Distinguish roles such as network engineer, programmer, support specialist, systems analyst, administrators, software developer, web developer and social-media specialist.

title: Assess ICT in major fields
points: Evaluate ICT in education, medicine, business, law enforcement and recreation.
Use examples such as distance learning, telemedicine, e-commerce, EPOS, telecommuting, surveillance, biometrics, music and gaming.

title: Create documents from different sources
points: Combine typed text, imported text, images and other objects in one document.
Keep imported content sized and positioned appropriately.

title: Use document formatting
points: Use font controls, colour, emphasis, tabs, bullets, numbering, spacing, alignment, highlighting and case appropriately.
Use page size, margins, breaks, numbering, headers, footers, footnotes and endnotes.

title: Edit and organise documents
points: Use block operations, search and replace, tables, borders, shading, row/column operations, split cells/tables, text direction, cell margins and columns.

title: Use review features
points: Use spelling and grammar tools, thesaurus, word count, language settings, comments and track changes to prepare a document for final use.

title: Protect documents
points: Use automatic save, backup copies and edit restrictions such as password protection.

title: Generate a table of contents
points: Use heading structure to build an automatic table of contents.
Place it appropriately and maintain meaningful heading levels.

title: Use mail merge
points: Create or use a primary document and data source.
Insert suitable field names and produce correctly merged output.

title: Create fillable forms
points: Use controls such as text boxes, check boxes, date pickers, drop-down lists and command buttons.
Design the form so it is clear and easy to use.

title: Plan a website
points: Define purpose, intended audience, number of pages, page content and layout before building.

title: Create simple web pages
points: Choose a suitable design and combine text and graphics.
Wrap text around images and create a home page with navigation.

title: Insert hyperlinks
points: Create links to another page, a location on the same page, an email address and a user-created file.

title: Evaluate a website
points: Check accuracy, user friendliness and effective display.
Verify links, use a test audience and keep content up to date.

title: Explain spreadsheet purpose
points: Use a spreadsheet to capture, display, calculate and manipulate tabular data.

title: Use spreadsheet terminology
points: Recognise workbook, worksheet, row, column, cell, cell address, range, label, value, formula and function.

title: Use predefined functions
points: Use SUM, AVERAGE, DATE, MAX, MIN, COUNT, COUNTA, COUNTIF, VLOOKUP, PMT and IF in appropriate situations.

title: Create arithmetic formulae
points: Build formulae using addition, subtraction, multiplication, division and brackets.
Apply correct operator order.

title: Copy formulae correctly
points: Distinguish relative and absolute references.
Use named ranges where appropriate and understand the effect of moving, copying and deleting cells.

title: Manipulate rows and columns
points: Insert, delete and modify rows and columns without losing the intended spreadsheet structure.

title: Manipulate spreadsheet data
points: Format numbers as currency, accounting, percentages and decimals.
Sort by primary and secondary fields, filter with multiple criteria and summarise data using one- and two-dimensional pivot tables, frequency distributions and pivot charts.

title: Perform charting operations
points: Choose column, bar, line or pie charts appropriately.
Use meaningful chart titles, axis labels and data labels.

title: Use multiple worksheets
points: Solve problems across one or more worksheets.
Link worksheets so related calculations update without unnecessary re-entry.

title: Explain database concepts
points: Understand a database as an organised repository of information and a collection of related tables.
Explain why databases are useful for structured records.

title: Use database terminology
points: Use table, record, field, primary key, secondary key, candidate key and foreign key correctly.
Choose numeric, text, logical, date/time and currency data types appropriately.

title: Create and relate database tables
points: Design tables using at least three data types and meaningful primary keys.
Modify field definitions and establish one-to-one and one-to-many relationships.

title: Manipulate database data
points: Use forms and subforms for data entry.
Build queries with multiple criteria, selected fields, calculated fields, relational operators and logical operators.
Create reports with sorting, grouping, COUNT, SUM and AVERAGE and send output to screen, printer or file.

title: Outline problem-solving steps
points: Define the problem, propose/evaluate solutions, choose an efficient solution, develop the algorithm, then test and validate it.

title: Use divide and conquer
points: Break a large everyday problem into smaller tasks, solve the parts and combine the solutions.

title: Define a problem using IPO
points: Identify the input, process and output for a problem.
Use an IPO chart to organise the solution.

title: Distinguish variables and constants
points: A variable can change during processing while a constant does not.
Use integer, real, character, Boolean and string types appropriately.

title: Explain algorithms
points: An algorithm should be finite, precise, unambiguous, have clear flow of control and terminate.

title: Represent algorithms
points: Use standard flowchart symbols and pseudocode.
Apply IF, IF-ELSE, nested conditions, FOR, WHILE and REPEAT.
Use relational, logical and arithmetic operators, including MOD and DIV, and understand truth tables.

title: Test algorithms
points: Use desk checks and dry runs.
Construct trace tables with identifiers as column headings and values recorded for each pass.

title: Distinguish language levels
points: Recognise machine/assembly as low-level languages and languages such as Visual Basic, Pascal and C as high-level examples.

title: Describe program implementation
points: Create source code, translate/link, execute/run and maintain the program.

title: Test and debug programs
points: Identify syntax, logic and runtime errors.
Use test data and debugging techniques to verify correctness.

title: Declare variables and constants
points: Use integer, real/double/float, character, string and Boolean/logical types in program declarations.

title: Translate algorithms into code
points: Use assignment, input/output, arithmetic, logical and relational operations.
Implement conditional branching and FOR, WHILE and REPEAT loops.

title: Document programs effectively
points: Use meaningful names, comments, indentation and whitespace for internal documentation.
Provide external documentation such as a user manual.
